description: Orphan allowlist for orphancheck/run.js. DENY BY DEFAULT: a key in `allow` means a human has triaged that orphan page (a published page in no navigation tree) and recorded what to do with it. Keys are the LOGICAL page key exactly as the gate reports it — `{component}[:{module}]/{relative-without-.adoc}`, e.g. "cloud:teams-and-users" or "hazelcast:clients/rest" — and one key covers that page across EVERY branch it is orphaned in. Each entry is an object with a required `disposition` and an optional one-line `note` (the audit trail): 'keep-in-nav' (will be added to the nav during migration, so it stops being an orphan), 'keep-referenced' (intentionally not in nav, reachable only via inline xref), 'redirect' (drop the page and redirect its old URL to a required destination, given as EITHER `to` -- a COMPONENT/VERSION-RELATIVE path such as "/maintain-cluster/rest-api", resolved against each version's own URL base so a version never redirects across a version boundary -- OR `toUrl`, an ABSOLUTE site route such as "/clc/5.5.1/overview", for the case where the only sensible destination is in ANOTHER component, which has its own version line and so offers no base to resolve against; give exactly one, and note that a `toUrl` pins a version elsewhere and so has to be revisited when that component's live set moves), or 'drop-404' (drop the page, a 404 is acceptable — nothing external should rely on it). Each entry may also carry `versions`: the version segments the decision applies in, e.g. ["5.5", "5.4"]. OMIT IT unless the page's orphan-ness genuinely DIFFERS between versions -- absent, the key covers every version, which is right whenever a page is an orphan wherever it exists. Present, it says the source itself differs: Platform 5.4 and 5.3 build ROOT/nav.adoc from per-module `include::<module>:partial$nav.adoc[]` partials and so still list pages the flat 5.5+ nav dropped, and six entries here would otherwise withhold a page those versions' own sidebar links to -- cluster-performance/performance-tuning worst of all, whose redirect target (performance-tips) does not exist at 5.3 at all. Matching is per version, so DENY BY DEFAULT applies per version too: the same page orphaned in a version the entry does not name is still flagged as untriaged. The list is hand-maintained and therefore drifts, so the gate reports any version named here that the page is in scope in and no longer an orphan in (trim it, do not delete the entry). Ships EMPTY: until an orphan's key is added here, the gate flags it.

clc:clc-cpmap.note: Real, substantial command-reference page (clc cpmap: get/set/put/remove/delete/destroy/compare-and-set), structurally identical to its clc-* siblings; it is simply MISSING from nav.adoc upstream -- a source omission, not a migration artifact, so it is invisible on the current Antora site too. Fixed AS PART OF THE MIGRATION: `nav.after` injects the entry into the parsed nav at conversion time (converter/lib/nav injectNavEntries), so buildPlan places it at clc/reference/clc-commands/clc-cpmap.mdx with a sidebar_position and no unlisted:true -- reproducible on every run, no hand-edit to be clobbered. Slug (/clc-cpmap) is URL-derived, so its URL is unchanged. Injected only where the page exists in that version (5.4.0+).

ACTED ON: the converter skips drop-404 pages, so no .mdx is emitted and the URL 404s; the gates drop it from scope rather than counting it as not-yet-converted.

User decision 2026-08-27: redirect to the CLC landing page -- exactly where the stub already sends readers. hazelcast:clients/rest.note: "REST Client" is a 9-line stub: one sentence telling the reader to see xref:maintain-cluster:rest-api.adoc for details, plus the shared rest-deprecation partial (the Community Edition REST API is deprecated and goes away at 7.0, superseded by the Enterprise REST API). NOTE the referrer deploy/enterprise-licenses deep-links to clients/rest#using-the-rest-endpoint-groups, an anchor that does not exist on the page today -- broken upstream already, and the fragment is dropped by the redirect. ACTED ON: the converter withholds redirect pages exactly as it does drop-404 ones (no .mdx is emitted, and the gates drop it from scope), and lib/dispositions redirectPairs resolves this `to` against the page's own URL base into a {from,to} in src/redirects.ts -- per version, so each version redirects within itself. The 7 inbound xrefs are retargeted at conversion time to point straight at rest-api, so the client redirect is left doing the job only it can: keeping the old URL alive for bookmarks and links from outside the site.
